items.title: Section: Fascicle 49 Opens the Chapter on the Grounds — Seven Grounds Named

items.zh: 如前所說十三住中，應知隨彼建立七地。前之六種，唯菩薩地；第七一種，菩薩、如來雜立為地。何等為七？一、種性地，二、勝解行地，三、淨勝意樂地，四、行正行地，五、決定地，六、決定行地，七、到究竟地。
items.en:
Within the Basic Section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the third yoga foundation of ultimate practice, the chapter on the grounds, part three.
Seventh chapter, the grounds; first, establishing the overall names; first, naming them. As previously explained across the thirteen abodes, one should understand that seven grounds are established corresponding to them. The first six belong solely to the bodhisattva; the seventh gathers bodhisattva and Tathāgata together as a single, mixed ground.
Second, posing the question. What are these seven?
Third, listing them. First, the lineage-ground. Second, the ground of resolute practice. Third, the ground of pure, excellent aspiration. Fourth, the ground of correct practice in conduct. Fifth, the ground of certainty. Sixth, the ground of certain conduct. Seventh, the ground of ultimate accomplishment.

items.title: Section: Mapping Seven Grounds Onto Thirteen Abodes — the Mixed Ground of Both Bodhisattva and Tathāgata

items.zh: 如是七種菩薩地中，最後一種名為雜地。前種姓住，名種性地；勝解行住，名勝解行地；極歡喜住，名淨勝意樂地；增上戒住、增上心住、三種增上慧住、有加行有功用無相住，名行正行地；無加行無功用無相住，名決定地，此地菩薩墮在第三決定中故；無礙解住，名決定行地；最上成滿菩薩住及如來住，名到究竟地。如來住地，於後建立佛法品中，當廣演說。
items.en:
Fourth, explaining; first, naming the final ground as mixed. Among these seven bodhisattva grounds, the last is called the mixed ground.
Second, mapping onto the bodhisattva's own abodes. The prior lineage-abode is called the lineage-ground. The abode of resolute practice is called the ground of resolute practice. The abode of utmost joy is called the ground of pure, excellent aspiration. The abode of heightened discipline, the abode of heightened mind, the three abodes of heightened wisdom, and the abode with applied effort having no further mark are together called the ground of correct practice in conduct. The abode without applied effort, without effortful application, having no further mark, is called the ground of certainty, since a bodhisattva at this abode falls within the third of the three kinds of certainty.
Commentary: Regarding "falls within the third kind of certainty" — the chapter on the qualities of a bodhisattva says: bodhisattvas fall, in brief, into three kinds of certainty. What are the three? First, certainty through abiding in the lineage. Second, certainty through arousing bodhicitta. Third, certainty through never practising in vain.
The abode of unobstructed understanding is called the ground of certain conduct. The abode of ultimate accomplishment together with the abode of the Tathāgata are together called the ground of ultimate accomplishment.
Third, pointing to the Tathāgata's own ground. The Tathāgata's own abiding-ground will be expounded at length in the later chapter on establishing the buddha-dharma.

items.title: Section: How a Bodhisattva First Becomes Forever Free of the Lower Realms — Compassion for a Hundred and Ten Kinds of Suffering

items.zh: 問：菩薩從勝解行地隨入淨勝意樂地時，云何超過諸惡趣等？答：是諸菩薩依止世間清淨靜慮，於勝解行地已善積集菩提資糧；於如前說百一十苦諸有情類修習哀愍，無餘思惟。由此修習為因緣故，於彼色類諸有情所，得哀愍意樂及悲意樂。
items.en:
Second, resolving a specific doubt; first, the question. Question: when a bodhisattva, passing from the ground of resolute practice, enters the ground of pure, excellent aspiration, how does such a bodhisattva transcend the lower realms of rebirth and the like?
Second, the answer; first, clarifying the cultivation; first, cultivating compassionate concern. Answer: such bodhisattvas, relying on worldly, purified meditative absorption, have, while at the ground of resolute practice, already well accumulated the provisions for awakening. Towards the hundred and ten kinds of suffering belonging to sentient beings already explained, such bodhisattvas cultivate compassionate concern, with no further reflection besides.
Commentary: Regarding "the hundred and ten kinds of suffering belonging to sentient beings" — the hundred and ten sufferings are as already explained in the earlier chapter on offering, drawing near, and the immeasurables. Observing that all experience is ultimately suffering, one cultivates the immeasurable quality of compassion; this is why it is said that compassionate concern is cultivated, with no further reflection besides.
Second, attaining compassionate aspiration. From this very cultivation as its cause and condition, towards embodied sentient beings of this kind, one attains compassionate concern and the aspiration of great compassion.

items.title: Section: Vowing to Dwell in the Lower Realms as One's Own Home — Suffering in Sentient Beings' Place

items.zh: 由是因緣，為利惡趣諸有情故，誓居惡趣如己舍宅。作是誓言：我若唯住如是處所，能證無上正等菩提，亦能忍受。為除一切有情苦故，一切有情諸惡趣業，以淨意樂，悉願自身代彼領受苦異熟果。為令畢竟一切惡業永不現行，一切善業常現行故，心發正願。
items.en:
Third, the mind gives rise to a correct vow. By this cause and condition, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings in the lower realms, such a bodhisattva vows to dwell in the lower realms as though dwelling in one's own home, making this vow: even should I, by dwelling in such places alone, be able to realise unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening, I would still be able to bear it. In order to remove every sentient being's own suffering, regarding every karma leading sentient beings to the lower realms, with pure aspiration, such a bodhisattva vows, in their place, to personally undergo the ripening-fruit of that very suffering — so that, ultimately, every unwholesome karma might never again manifest, and every wholesome karma might constantly manifest; the mind gives rise to this correct vow.
Commentary: Regarding "with pure aspiration" — arousing, towards sentient beings, an aspiration for their benefit and ease is wholesome, and is for this reason called pure — not because it is subsumed within undefiled, world-transcending meditative absorption.

items.title: Section: The Underlying Tendency Eliminated — A Transformed Basis, and Three Names for One Attainment

items.zh: 彼由修習如是世間清淨靜慮悲願力故，一切惡趣諸煩惱品所有麁重，於自所依皆得除遣。由此斷故，菩薩不久獲得轉依，於諸惡趣所有惡業畢竟不作，於諸惡趣決定不往。齊此菩薩，說名超過一切惡趣，亦名超過勝解行地，亦名已入淨勝意樂地。
items.en:
Second, clarifying transcendence; first, severing coarse dross. Through the power of this worldly, purified meditative absorption together with this compassionate vow, every coarse residue belonging to every affliction connected with the lower realms is entirely removed from its own underlying basis.
Second, attaining a transformed basis. Because of this severing, such a bodhisattva, before long, attains a transformed basis — ultimately never again performing any deed leading to the lower realms, and never again, with certainty, going there.
Third, concluding with alternate names. A bodhisattva who has reached this point is said to have transcended every lower realm, is also said to have transcended the ground of resolute practice, and is also said to have already entered the ground of pure, excellent aspiration.

items.title: Section: The Same Ten Purifying Dharmas, Now Applied to the Ordinary Bodhisattva Before the First Ground

items.zh: 如前住品所說信等能淨修治諸住十法，今於此中，當知亦能淨修治地。如是十法所有安立所治、能治略義次第，皆應了知。謂彼十種淨修地法，能對治彼所對治法，故得安立。何等為十？謂一切種全未發心，全未受持菩薩學處，是名為信所對治法；對治彼故，安立於信。
items.en:
Third, displaying the dharmas that purify; first, the overall statement. As already explained in the earlier chapter on the abodes, faith and the rest are ten dharmas able to purify every abode; one should understand that, here too, they are equally able to purify these grounds. Every one of these ten dharmas' own manner of establishment, what each remedies, what each serves as remedy, and their own brief meaning and sequence, should all be understood.
Commentary: Regarding "as already explained in the earlier chapter on the abodes, faith and the rest are ten dharmas" — the ten dharmas already explained, namely pure faith, compassion, loving-kindness, generous giving, freedom from weariness, mastering treatises, understanding the world, cultivating conscientiousness, firm resolve, and offering to the Tathāgata, are entirely identical to those here. Yet that earlier purification addressed only the noble grounds, while this passage addresses specifically what precedes the first ground; this is why the meaning here differs. Everything explained below regarding establishment, remedy, and sequence concerns specifically the lineage-ground and the ground of resolute practice, not extending to any of the remaining higher grounds, since those higher grounds' own mark has already been explained in the earlier chapter on the abodes; this is why it is not repeated here in full.
Second, explaining individually; first, establishment; first, naming it. These ten dharmas purifying the ground are established precisely because each is able to remedy its own corresponding thing to be remedied.
Second, posing the question. What are the ten?
Third, explaining; first, faith. Namely, entirely, in every kind, not yet having aroused bodhicitta at all, and entirely not yet having undertaken the bodhisattva's own training whatsoever — this is called what faith remedies; remedying this, faith is established.

items.title: Section: Compassion, Loving-Kindness, Giving, and Tirelessness — Remedying an Ordinary Being's Own Harmful Intent, Anger, Attachment, and Self-Interest

items.zh: 於諸有情有損害心，是名為悲所對治法；對治彼故，安立於悲。於諸有情有瞋恚心，是名為慈所對治法；對治彼故，安立於慈。於身命財有所顧戀，是名為捨所對治法；對治彼故，安立於捨。於諸有情悕求報恩，見彼邪行貪著利養多有所作，是無厭倦所對治法；對治彼故，安立無倦。
items.en:
Second, compassion. Harbouring the intent to harm sentient beings is called what compassion remedies; remedying this, compassion is established.
Third, loving-kindness. Harbouring anger and hatred towards sentient beings is called what loving-kindness remedies; remedying this, loving-kindness is established.
Fourth, giving. Harbouring attachment to one's own body, life, and wealth is called what giving remedies; remedying this, giving is established.
Fifth, freedom from weariness. Hoping for repayment from sentient beings, or, upon seeing their wrongful conduct, undertaking much effort out of attachment to gain, is called what freedom from weariness remedies; remedying this, freedom from weariness is established.
Commentary: Regarding "hoping for repayment from sentient beings" and the like — hoping for repaid kindness, one undertakes much effort towards beings. Or, seeing their wrongful conduct, and further attached to gain as one's own cause and condition, one undertakes much effort. This obstructs the undertaking of benefiting others, preventing its completion; this is why it is said to be what freedom from weariness remedies.

items.title: Section: Mastering Treatises, Understanding the World, Conscientiousness, Firm Resolve, Offering to the Tathāgata

items.zh: 無有方便善巧加行，是善知論所對治法；對治彼故，立善知論。性不柔和，不於他心隨順而轉，是名善知一切世間所對治法；對治彼故，安立善知一切世間。於修善法放逸懈怠，是名慚愧所對治法；對治彼故，安立慚愧。於其長時種種猛利無間無斷生死大苦深生怯弱，當知是名堅力持性所對治法；對治彼故，所以安立堅力持性。於大師所猶豫疑惑，當知是名供養如來所對治法；對治彼故，所以安立供養如來。如是且說所治、能治安立十法。
items.en:
Sixth, mastering treatises. Lacking any skilful means or applied effort is called what mastering treatises remedies; remedying this, mastering treatises is established.
Seventh, understanding the world. A disposition that is not gentle, unable to turn according to others' own hearts, is called what understanding the world remedies; remedying this, understanding the world is established.
Eighth, conscientiousness. Laxity and indolence in cultivating wholesome dharmas is called what conscientiousness remedies; remedying this, conscientiousness is established.
Ninth, firm resolve. Deep timidity before the long, fierce, uninterrupted great suffering of birth-and-death is called what firm resolve remedies; remedying this, firm resolve is established.
Tenth, offering to the Tathāgata. Hesitation and doubt regarding the great teacher is called what offering to the Tathāgata remedies; remedying this, offering to the Tathāgata is established.
Fourth, the conclusion. This, in brief, explains the establishment of these ten dharmas through what each remedies and how each serves as remedy.

blocks.text: Fascicle 49 opens the chapter on grounds. It retells the path in seven grounds instead of thirteen abodes, then explains how a bodhisattva leaves the lower realms behind forever.

Lineage, resolute practice, pure excellent aspiration, correct practice, certainty, certain conduct, and arrival at the ultimate. "The first six belong solely to the bodhisattva; the seventh sets bodhisattva and Tathāgata together." Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary bodhisattvas occupy the first two. Venerable Miào Jìng: "abode" means according, "ground" means producing.
Master Cháng Bǎi: whatever is cultivated is never wasted; one is certain to become a buddha.

Master Cháng Bǎi: in worldly purified absorption, craving, views, pride, doubt, and ignorance do not manifest, but their seeds are not cut. The bodhisattva cultivates compassion "towards beings in the hundred and ten sufferings already described" (Day 395).

subs.head: The lower realms as one's home

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: as if there were nowhere else but the three lower realms, like living in one's own home. Master Cháng Bǎi: if you cannot yet do this, learn from Master Hóngyī and vow to bear it in the future.

Master Cháng Bǎi: all the coarse seeds that lead to the lower realms are removed from one's own aggregates; without that cause, no condition can bring a lower rebirth. Venerable Miào Jìng: making no evil cause, one receives no evil result.

subs.head: The ten purifying dharmas, before the grounds

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: the names are the same as on the first ground, the meaning differs: one is ordinary, one noble. "Not having aroused the aspiration at all … is what faith remedies." Master Cháng Bǎi: faith is the source of the path, the mother of merits.

Venerable Miào Jìng, on anger: telling someone "Don't be upset!" helps about as much as nothing; no one should laugh at anyone, since we all have these afflictions. "Attachment to one's body, life, and wealth is what giving remedies."
Venerable Miào Jìng, on stubbornness: "I stick to my own ideas; I'll do as I please." Master Cháng Bǎi: understanding any worldly matter (cooking, driving, healing, consoling) is learning.

Master Hóngyī (1880–1942), the artist who became a Vinaya master, often wrote out a line from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*: "not seeking comfort for myself, only wishing beings free of suffering". Master Cháng Bǎi's point is gentle: if we cannot yet bear it, we can at least vow to.

quiz.q: Why is the last of the seven grounds called "mixed"?
options: the first six are bodhisattva grounds only; the seventh sets bodhisattva and Tathāgata together
quiz.why: "The first six belong solely to the bodhisattva; the seventh sets bodhisattva and Tathāgata together." Master Cháng Bǎi: the two states are spoken of together, hence "mixed."

quiz.q: What are the seven grounds in order?
options: lineage, resolute practice, pure aspiration, correct practice, certainty, certain conduct, ultimate
quiz.why: Lineage, resolute practice, pure excellent aspiration, correct practice, certainty, certain conduct, and arrival at the ultimate. Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary bodhisattvas occupy the first two.

quiz.q: How do the lectures distinguish "abode" and "ground"?
options: both: abode means accord, ground means producing — Cháng Bǎi: according with suchness, subsequent wisdom produces merit and wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "abode" means according, "ground" means producing. Master Cháng Bǎi: noble bodhisattvas' prajñā accords with suchness; subsequent wisdom resting on the ultimate produces merit and wisdom.

quiz.q: "The ground of certainty — fallen into the third certainty." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the third certainty?
options: whatever is cultivated is never in vain — certain to become a buddha
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: whatever is cultivated is never wasted, not in vain — certain to become a buddha. Venerable Miào Jìng: resolute, of great accomplishment, not in vain.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "worldly purified absorption"?
options: no affliction manifests, but seeds remain uncut
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: no afflictions such as craving, views, pride, doubt, and ignorance manifest, but their seeds are not cut — that is worldly purified absorption. Venerable Miào Jìng: not the world-transcending purity that eliminates afflictions.

quiz.q: What is the object of the bodhisattva's cultivation of compassion here?
options: beings in the hundred and ten sufferings, with no other thought
quiz.why: "Towards beings in the hundred and ten sufferings already described, cultivating compassion, with no other thought." Master Cháng Bǎi: all three feelings are suffering, so one cultivates immeasurable compassion.

quiz.q: The bodhisattva vows to live in the lower realms as at home, and to bear beings' suffering. How do the lectures view this?
options: Miào Jìng: if only the lower realms were available, living there as at home; Cháng Bǎi: their suffering doesn't obstruct the vow — if not yet able, vow like Hongyi to bear it later
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: supposing there were nowhere else but the three lower realms — like living in one's own home. Master Cháng Bǎi: their suffering doesn't obstruct the vow; if not yet able, learn from Master Hongyi and vow to bear it in the future.

quiz.q: On attaining the transformed basis, which three names apply?
options: surpassing the lower realms, surpassing resolute practice, entering pure aspiration
quiz.why: "At this point the bodhisattva is said to surpass all lower realms, to surpass the ground of resolute practice, and to have entered the ground of pure aspiration." Venerable Miào Jìng: making no evil cause, one receives no evil result.

options: not having aroused the aspiration at all, not having taken up bodhisattva training
quiz.why: "Not having aroused the aspiration at all, not having taken up the bodhisattva trainings, is what faith remedies." Venerable Miào Jìng: with faith one arouses bodhicitta and takes precepts. Master Cháng Bǎi: faith is the source of the path, mother of merits.

options: attachment to body, life, and wealth
quiz.why: "Attachment to one's body, life, and wealth is what giving remedies." Master Cháng Bǎi: cherishing body and life blocks diligent practice; cherishing wealth makes one stingy.
